title: How the Word makes the Father known
source_text: Διόπερ ἐὰν ἔρηται ἡμᾶς Κέλσος, πῶς οἰόμεθα γνωρίζειν τὸν θεὸν, καὶ πῶς πρὸς αὐτὸν σωθήσεσθαι· ἀποκρινούμεθα ὅτι ἱκανός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος, γενόμενος τοῖς ζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἢ τοῖς ἐπιφαινόμενον αὐτὸν παραδεχομένοις, γνωρίσαι καὶ ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν πατέρα, πρὸ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ οὐχ ὁρώμενον. τίς δ᾿ ἄλλος σῶσαι καὶ προσαγαγεῖν τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ δύναται τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ψυχὴν ἢ ὁ θεὸς λόγος; ὅστις „ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν“ ὢν διὰ τοὺς κολληθέντας τῇ σαρκὶ καὶ γενομένους ὅπερ „σὰρξ“ „ἐγένετο“ „σὰρξ,“ ἵνα χωρηθῇ ὑπὸ τῶν μὴ δυναμένων αὐτὸν βλέπειν καθὸ „λόγος“ ἦν καὶ „πρὸς θεὸν“ ἦν „καὶ θεὸς ἦν.“ καὶ σωματικῶς γε λαλούμενος καὶ ὡς „σὰρξ“ ἀπαγγελλόμενος ἐφ᾿ ἑαυτὸν καλεῖ τοὺς ὄντας σάρκα, ἵν᾿ αὐτοὺς ποιήσῃ πρῶτον μορφωθῆναι κατὰ λόγον τὸν γενόμενον σάρκα, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὺς ἀναβιβάσῃ ἐπὶ τὸ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν, ὅπερ ἦν πρὶν γένηται „σάρξ“· ὥστε αὐτοὺς ὠφεληθέντας καὶ ἀναβάντας ἀπὸ τῆς κατὰ σάρκα εἰσαγωγῆς εἰπεῖν τό· „εἰ καὶ Χριστόν ποτε κατὰ σάρκα ἐγνώκαμεν, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν.“ „σὰρξ“ οὖν „ἐγένετο,“ καὶ γενόμενος „σὰρξ“ „ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν“ οὐκ ἔξω γινόμενος ἡμῶν, σκηνώσας δὲ καὶ γενόμενος ἐν ἡμῖν οὐκ ἔμεινεν ἐπὶ τῆς πρώτης μορφῆς, ἀλλ᾿ ἀναβιβάσας ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸ λογικὸν „ὑψηλὸν ὄρος“ ἔδειξεν ἡμῖν τὴν ἔνδοξον μορφὴν ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τὴν λαμπρότητα τῶν ἐνδυμάτων αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐχ ἑαυτοῦ γε μόνου ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦ πνευματικοῦ γε νόμου, ὅς ἐστιν „ἐν δόξῃ“ ὀφθεὶς μετὰ Ἰησοῦ „Μωϋσῆς“. ἔδειξε δ᾿ ἡμῖν καὶ πᾶσαν προφητείαν, οὐδὲ μετὰ τὸ ἐνανθρωπῆσαι ἀποθνῄσκουσαν ἀλλ᾿ ἀναλαμβανομένην εἰς οὐρανὸν, ἧς σύμβολον Ἠλίας ἦν. ὁ δὲ ταῦτα θεωρήσας εἴποι ἂν τό· „ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρὸς, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας.“ Κέλσος μὲν οὖν ἰδιωτικώτερον ἀνέπλασεν ἃ οἴεται ἡμᾶς λέξειν πρὸς τὸ πύσμα αὐτοῦ· πῶς οἰόμεθα γνωρίσειν τὸν θεὸν, καὶ πῶς σωθήσεσθαι πρὸς αὐτόν; ἡμεῖς δὲ εἴποιμεν ἂν τὰ προεκκείμενα.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore (διόπερ) if Celsus asks (ἔρομαι) us how we think (οἴομαι) to know (γνωρίζω) God, and how to be saved (σῴζω, fut. σωθήσεσθαι) toward him (πρὸς αὐτόν); we shall answer that sufficient (ἱκανός) is the Word (λόγος) of God, having come (γενόμενος) to those seeking (ζητέω) him or to those receiving (παραδέχομαι) him appearing (ἐπιφαίνομαι), to make known (γνωρίζω) and reveal (ἀποκαλύπτω) the Father, before his coming (παρουσία) not being seen (ὁράω). Who else is able to save and bring to (προσάγω) the God over all (ὁ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεός) the soul (ψυχή) of man, than God the Word (ὁ θεὸς λόγος)? Who, being 'in the beginning with God', on account of those glued (κολλάω) to the flesh (σάρξ) and become what flesh is, 'became flesh', that he might be contained/received (χωρέω) by those unable to see him insofar as (καθό) he was 'Word' and was 'with God' 'and was God'. And being spoken (λαλέω) bodily (σωματικῶς) and announced (ἀπαγγέλλω) as 'flesh', he calls to himself those being flesh, that he may make them first be formed (μορφόω) according to the Word become flesh, and after this lead them up (ἀναβιβάζω) to seeing him as he was before he became 'flesh'; so that they, benefited (ὠφελέω) and having ascended (ἀναβαίνω) from the introduction (εἰσαγωγή) according to flesh, say: 'Even if we once knew Christ according to flesh, yet now we no longer know.' 'Flesh' then he 'became', and become flesh he 'tabernacled (σκηνόω) in/among us', not coming to be outside (ἔξω) us; having tabernacled and come to be in us he did not remain in the first form (μορφή), but having led us up onto the rational/of-the-Word (λογικόν) 'high mountain' he showed us his glorious (ἔνδοξος) form and the brightness (λαμπρότης) of his garments (ἔνδυμα), and not of himself only but also of the spiritual (πνευματικός) law (νόμος), which is 'Moses' seen 'in glory' with Jesus. He showed us also all prophecy (προφητεία), not dying (ἀποθνῄσκω) even after he became man (ἐνανθρωπέω) but being taken up (ἀναλαμβάνω) into heaven, of which Elijah was the symbol (σύμβολον). He who has contemplated (θεωρέω) these would say: 'We beheld (θεάομαι) his glory, glory as of an only-begotten (μονογενής) from the Father, full of grace (χάρις) and truth (ἀλήθεια).' Celsus then more amateurishly (ἰδιωτικώτερον) fabricated (ἀναπλάσσω) what he thinks we will say to his inquiry (πύσμα): how we think we shall know God and how be saved toward him? But we would say the things set out before (προεκκείμενα).
pass_b_english: So if Celsus asks us how we think we come to know God, and how we shall be saved and brought to him, we will answer that the Word of God is able, when he comes to those who seek him or to those who receive him when he appears, to make known and to reveal the Father (Matthew 11:27), who was not seen before his coming. Who else can save the soul of man and bring it to the God who is over all, except God the Word? He was “in the beginning with God” (John 1:2), and for the sake of those who had clung to the flesh and become what flesh is, he “became flesh” (John 1:14), so that he might be received by those who could not see him in so far as he was “the Word,” and was “with God,” “and was God” (John 1:1).

And being spoken of in bodily terms and proclaimed as “flesh,” he calls to himself those who are flesh, so that he may first make them be formed after the Word who became flesh, and after this lead them up to see him as he was before he became “flesh.” In this way, once they have been helped and have climbed up from the first lessons according to the flesh, they may say: “Even though we once knew Christ according to the flesh, yet now we no longer know him in that way” (2 Corinthians 5:16).

He “became flesh,” then, and having become “flesh” he “dwelt among us” (John 1:14), not coming to be outside us. And having dwelt and come to be among us, he did not stay in his first form. He led us up onto the “high mountain” (Matthew 17:1) of the Word and showed us his glorious form and the brightness of his garments (Matthew 17:2), and not his own only, but also that of the spiritual law, which is “Moses,” seen “in glory” with Jesus (Luke 9:30–31). He showed us also the whole of prophecy, which did not die even after he became man, but was taken up into heaven; Elijah was its symbol (2 Kings 2:11). And one who has gazed on these things could say: “We beheld his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth” (John 1:14).

Celsus, then, has made up in a rather crude way what he thinks we will say to his question, how we think we shall come to know God and how we shall be saved and brought to him. But we would say what has been set out above.

choices.choice: Matthew 11:27 is cited as a clear allusion (the Word reveals the Father); ‘not seen before his coming’ may also recall John 1:18, left uncited. John 1:14 is quoted three times (became flesh; dwelt among us; we beheld his glory). ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν is rendered ‘dwelt among us’; Origen’s gloss οὐκ ἔξω γινόμενος ἡμῶν (‘not coming to be outside us’) plays on ἐν ἡμῖν, which can also mean ‘in us’. τὸ λογικὸν ὑψηλὸν ὄρος: λογικόν (rational, belonging to the Word) is rendered ‘the high mountain of the Word’; ‘the rational high mountain’ is the bare sense. Transfiguration: Matthew 17:1-2 for the high mountain and shining garments (also Mark 9:2-3, Luke 9:29); ‘seen in glory’ (ὀφθεὶς ... ἐν δόξῃ) matches Luke 9:31 (οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ). Elijah taken up into heaven: 2 Kings 2:11 = LXX 4 Kingdoms 2:11. 2 Corinthians 5:16 rendered ‘we no longer know him in that way’ to keep οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν with its implied object. The TEI repeats ‘σὰρξ’ before ‘ἐγένετο σάρξ’ as Origen’s play on ‘became what flesh is’; followed. ‘Celsus’s question’ (πύσμα) refers back to 6.66. πρὸς αὐτὸν σωθήσεσθαι rendered ‘be saved and brought to him’ (σῴζω with πρός: come safely to), matching Origen’s own reply ‘save and bring to the God over all’. καθὸ λόγος ἦν rendered ‘in so far as he was the Word’. μορφωθῆναι κατὰ λόγον rendered ‘be formed after the Word’. ἰδιωτικώτερον rendered ‘in a rather crude way’ (like a layman).
'saved by going to him' to 'saved and brought to him' twice (πρὸς αὐτὸν σωθήσεσθαι; 'by going' added a means not in the Greek)
'see him as he was the Word' to 'see him in so far as he was "the Word"' (καθό; the old wording was ambiguous; 'Word' put in quotation marks as in the Greek)
'take the form of the Word' to 'be formed after the Word' (μορφωθῆναι κατὰ λόγον: formed according to, not turned into)
2 Corinthians 5:16 'we know him so no longer' to 'we no longer know him in that way' (stiff)
'in a rather amateur way' to 'in a rather crude way' (ἰδιωτικώτερον)
